commit_note: The rows were produced by the harness at e12aceb4bba, which is the tip of the branch when the measurement ran. The commits after it change the plan document and the text of this file, not the measurement path. The trees that produce these rows are in b5ce6b3c1d5, which marked the collection buffers transient so a dataset written by another ROOT build can be opened at all.

supersedes.reason: The superseded artifact measured a build from before the collection buffers were added to TTree. Those members were not transient, so the streamer read them from the file and the dataset could not be opened at all until b5ce6b3c1d5 marked them transient. Its rows are therefore not reproducible on the current branch, and its mapped row at 1.061 s sits below every later sample of the same row.

environment.machine: macOS (Apple Silicon), 10 cores, 32 GiB RAM, local out-of-source build root-build-tagma
environment.build: Release, treeplayer=ON, dataframe=ON, testing=ON, ROOT 6.41.01, builtin gtest
environment.dataset_note: CMS Run2016G DoubleMuon NanoAOD, tree Events, 2,315,223 events, 2,155,974,646 bytes, downloaded from eospublic.cern.ch as 05DD095C-F6C3-9A4F-9FB3-348A5A6403D5.root and held under the name above
environment.uncompressed: /Users/blackgene/Documents/nanoaod/cms_nanoaod_uncompressed.root, the same tree written with compression 0, 10,862,697,517 bytes
environment.store: /Users/blackgene/Documents/nanoaod/tagma_store.bin, 5,926,970,880 bytes, checksum 233,262,869,086, written by tagma_make_store.C, 2,560-byte records holding the first 320 scalar leaves as doubles

protocol.warm: tagma_bench reads each local source through the page cache in an untimed pass before the timed pass (warm_cache=1, the default), so every row measures the read path against resident data. Without this pass the row order decides the result: a pass over the 10.86 GB uncompressed rewrite evicts the 5.93 GB store. tagma_columns and tagma_rdf_columns have no such pass and were run after a shell-level read of the source.
protocol.order: within a run the rows are measured in a fixed order: baseline, baseline_uncomp, coordinate, coordinate+map
protocol.samples: the full-file rows are three consecutive steady-state runs. Three earlier runs on a settling page cache measured baseline 248.979, 202.469, 182.609 and coordinate 2.874, 2.689, 2.685; they are recorded in the notes and excluded from the ranges.
protocol.single_run_rows: the control rows and the RDataFrame rows are one warmed run each
protocol.baseline: the fork's ordinary read path with no store attached: the coordinate hooks are dormant null checks when no store is present, and the branch, basket, cache, and file layers are unchanged from upstream
protocol.metrics: wall and cpu seconds from TStopwatch, read calls from TFile::GetReadCalls, store-served calls from TFile::GetTagmaReadCalls, read syscalls from TFile::GetSysReadCalls, bytes moved from TFile::GetBytesRead
protocol.checksum: the served bytes of both coordinate rows match the conversion checksum 233,262,869,086 in every sampled run

synthetic_20k.note: synthetic scattered tree with the same per-event payload, 20,000 events, 3 branches per event, cache disabled. The coordinate rows run 20,000 aligned reads of 51 MB, so the 0.03 to 0.08 s scale is dominated by per-syscall cost and the ratios below are indicative only.
synthetic_20k.structural: 3.00 reads and 3.00 syscalls per event on the baseline against 1.00 and 1.00 on the coordinate row, and 0.00 syscalls on the mapped row

real_same_media_2k.note: local NanoAOD file, 2,000 events, cache disabled, the M1 signature slice. Three runs. The coordinate walls are sub-millisecond, so the ratios are indicative.
real_same_media_2k.structural: baseline 1.37 reads and 1.37 syscalls per event at 2,635 bytes per read against 1.00 and 1.00 at 2,560 bytes, and 0.00 syscalls on the mapped row

real_same_media_full.note: local NanoAOD file, all 2,315,223 events, cache disabled, sources warmed before each timed pass. Three steady-state runs; each row is a range over the runs.

real_remote_2k.note: not re-measured in this artifact. The row read the remote EOS file through the network plugin, and the media is the subject there rather than the read path. The superseded artifact recorded baseline 100.105 s wall at 1.160 s cpu, coordinate 0.002 s, coordinate_map 0.000 s over 2,000 events.

controls.note: tagma_columns.C on the same file and machine, one warmed run, cache disabled except where stated. The store's columns are the 320 field names of the layout sidecar.

rdf.note: tagma_rdf_columns.C, ROOT 6.41.01, one warmed run, the second run of each query reported so JIT compilation is outside the timing. The layout sidecar reports 320 store columns, of which 276 are variable-length arrays and 44 are scalar leaves.

analysis.note: tagma_bench analysis mode, warmed, one run: the same selection (MET_pt above 100 GeV and at least one muon) and the same MET_pt histogram on both read paths over the events the store covers. The layout sidecar maps the two selected columns onto the record.
analysis.reads_store: the store's cost on the two selected columns is 2.715 s against 2.698 s for the whole record in the same session, which is the column independence the store claims: the record is the addressing unit

phases_2_6.note: Measured after the phase-1 rows above, on the same machine and the same dataset. The rows live in the harness record at the top of benchmarks/tagma/tagma_harness.C, the master document; this section carries them into the tracked artifact. Each entry names the tool that produced it and the layer the row reads at, because the phase-1 rows, the index rows, and the entry rows are not layer-matched and the difference decides what each row supports.

collection_store.fields: 974 scalar fields and 406 array fields in 19 collections, every one of the tree's 1,380 leaves, with the leaf types preserved instead of widened to double; index record 1,280 bytes, data region 4,118,805,545 bytes, payload 7,082,290,985 bytes, 2,315,223 events, conversion 1,963.3 s
collection_store.layer: the read path reads the index record and the event's slice, 2.00 reads per event, with no field delivery
collection_store.note: the delivery the branches cost is about 50 microseconds per event, which is the whole difference between the 10.2 s read path and the 117.6 s whole-event row; the scalar-only rows leave the collection branches disabled and are served from the index record alone, 42 to 54 times the baseline
collection_store.crossover: against RDataFrame on the same file with a warm cache the column sum runs 0.132 s at one column, 1.716 s at eight, 7.411 s at 32, 16.806 s at 64 and 139.798 s at the whole 974 scalar columns; the 10.2 s read path crosses that ramp near 42 columns and the 117.6 s whole-event row near 810, both by first-order interpolation between the measured points

compression.blocks: 256 KB blocks, zlib level 1, 27,017 blocks, written in 75.4 s
compression.note: the read path on its own is the whole payload through the byte source with no entry layer, 572 MB/s; compression keeps that advantage and shrinks the file. The compressed whole-event row with the branches active, 197.6 s, is the delivery layer and not the read path. A block size of 8 KB, carried in the descriptor, moves the index-record scattered read from 222 to 16 microseconds per event and the file from 2.897 to 2.990 GB, 2.44 to 2.37 times

scatter.protocol: 2,000 events in list order, same medium, the 8 KB block store, one run; the baseline drives TTree::GetEntry with no branch addresses, so it delivers nothing into analysis variables, and the entry rows deliver all 1,380 field branches, so they are payload-matched and layer-matched with the baseline
scatter.gate: before they are timed the entry rows are compared with the baseline file over 32 sampled entries on the delivered event and MET_pt values; the gate passed with no mismatch
scatter.basket_boundary: the first basket of the measured file covers entries 0 to 999, and a scattered list inside it reads like a scan, 6 requests at 500 and at 1,000 events, 0.076 to 0.093 s; a list that spans a second basket collapses, 1,365,153 requests at 2,000 events, because a jump between baskets invalidates the current basket of each of the 1,380 branches. The penalty is a boundary, not a slope, and the store's count is flat across it
scatter.note: the store's whole-event per-event cost is 50 microseconds, the figure the collection-store scan rows measure, which places the store's remaining cost in the delivery layer rather than in the read path

threads.layer: every worker with its own file object and a disjoint range; the store row reads the whole payload through the block source, the baseline rows drive GetEntry with no branch addresses, so all rows move the data with no field copy
threads.note: the store scales 4.6 times and the cache-less baseline 5.8 over eight threads, so the lead narrows from 14.3 to 11.2 rather than widening: the store is bandwidth bound and the baseline I/O bound. The per-worker cache neither helps nor hurts, because each worker reads a contiguous range. This machine has ten cores, so the row ends at eight and O(128) is an extrapolation, not a measurement

derived_ratios.payload_equal_basis: the uncompressed row with the store's columns active, 35.935 s, which moves 6,127,346,663 bytes against the store's 5,926,970,880, so it moves 3.4 percent more bytes than the store; the coordinate rows are the mean of the three steady-state runs, 2.745 and 1.577
derived_ratios.best_config_basis: the same columns on the compressed file with the 32 MB cache, 111.111 s, ROOT's best configuration for the store's payload
derived_ratios.rdf_two_columns_basis: RDataFrame reads the two columns of the analysis workload in 0.558 s; the store reads the same two columns in 2.715 s, and that is also what it spends on the whole record, so its cost does not depend on the columns selected
derived_ratios.crossover_basis: the store's full-record cost divided by RDataFrame's marginal cost per column, (10.849 - 0.558) / 42 = 0.245 s, against 2.745 s and 1.577 s. First order from the measured points, not a fitted model.

notes: The baseline is stable across the three steady-state runs, 187.0 to 188.2 s wall and 183.6 to 185.9 s cpu. The first three runs after the page cache had been disturbed measured 248.979, 202.469 and 182.609 s, so a settling cache moves the baseline by up to a third.

Warming the sources is what makes the coordinate rows reproducible: 2.706, 2.722 and 2.808 s warmed against 2.793, 3.56 and 4.047 s across the unwarmed runs of the superseded artifact and the later control set.

Decompression removal is worth 2.20 to 2.31x of the baseline, not the 1.74x of the superseded artifact. That artifact divided by an uncompressed row of 117.86 s measured on a cold file; the warmed row is 81.1 to 85.7 s. The remaining wall time is the read path.

The mapped row is 116.6 to 120.5x, not the 181.7x of the superseded artifact. That row measured 1.061 s there against 1.55 to 1.61 s in the three warmed runs here and 1.71 to 1.79 s in the unwarmed runs, so 1.061 s is the low outlier of nine samples and the condition that produced it was not recorded. The ratio it implies is not reproduced.

The head of the store's advantage is column independence: the store reads the whole record for 2.745 s whatever the analysis selects, while RDataFrame spends 0.558 s on two columns and 10.849 s on the 44 scalar columns. Above about 11 columns, or about 6 with the store mapped, the store is ahead.
The two-column row is the store's weakest case and is stated as such: RDataFrame is 4.92x faster there.

The synthetic and 2,000-event rows are microbenchmark scale. Their coordinate walls are 0.03 to 0.08 s and 0.001 to 0.003 s, where per-syscall cost and timer resolution dominate, so their ratios are not stable claims. What is stable there is the request and system call count per event.
No end-to-end reproduction of the documented 14-hour production workload; these are full-dataset local measurements on one machine, single core, and the remote row was not re-measured.

The store's columns are the first 320 scalar leaves as doubles. Of the tree's 1,380 leaves, 276 of those 320 columns are variable-length arrays stored through their leading element, so the store's payload is a scalar projection rather than the full event. Carrying the collections is the work the reader backend now supports; this artifact predates a store written that way.

The section phases_2_6 records the measurements made after this artifact: the collection store, its compression, the event-selected rows, and the thread scaling. The phase-1 rows above are unchanged and remain the record of the projection. The scatter section is the one that decides the claim, and it states its layer: the entry rows read the whole event with the fields delivered, and the ratio they support is 2,000 times, not the five orders an index-record row against a whole-event baseline would suggest.
